column1: # The attack matrix's expected outcomes (ci/attack-matrix.sh, #215, #326): one line per attempt in
# ci/attack/attack.sh, `<attempt>\t<outcome>`, compared exactly. GOT (an escape) is never expected.
# A change in what wicket allows shows up here, in review. Outcomes: ci/attack/attack.sh's header.
# controls: what the zone allows works (a control that fails is a FAIL, not an escape)
# through the proxy, outside the zone: other hosts, methods, request shapes, the host's own addresses,
# loopback in its spellings, cloud metadata, IP literals, wicket's own ports, names whose DNS answers
# are internal (*.nip.io and localtest.me are in reach: the dial check refuses them), other ports
# path tricks against the reach rules (the echo host shows the path the upstream saw: contained means
# within the rule, as the upstream reads it)
# the injected credential reflected (#362): contained here; the host checks each body for the canary,
# around the proxy: no proxy, raw TCP and UDP, the forwarder's ports, the synthetic addresses' other
# ports, DNS (wicket's resolver answers only from its synthetic range), raw and packet sockets, frames
# written straight to the forwarder's UDP relay, the host's unix and abstract sockets
# the forwarder's host sockets spoken to directly, and the model proxy (a program has no model route)
# the gateway's tools: asking files a request for a human (asked) and grants nothing; deciding,
# renewing, spawning, linking, connecting, capacity, updates and messages; prefix and standing asks
# a prefix grant an operator made (ci/attack-matrix.sh approves it): within it is contained, any way out
# files outside the box's volumes: the host's, wicket's data directory, the run directories, the vault;
# symlinks to host paths left where the host reads (the host checks they weren't followed); read-only
